A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the Visual Haystacks benchmark and MIRAGE framework. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite extensive revision and a changed title.

before.justification: V1 reports original VHs evaluations, MIRAGE results on RetVQA and single-image benchmarks, positional-bias experiments, and compression and retrieval analyses.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark evaluations and diagnostic experiments in Figures 2–4, Tables 1–2, and appendix Tables C.1–C.2, including results for the revised MIRAGE model.

M1.justification: V1 uses a Vicuna backbone and a single-layer MLP retriever operating on pooled query/image features; v2 uses Llama-v3.1-8B and several transformer blocks for retrieval. V2 also introduces pretraining data annealing and changes the relevant-image-only training phase from 75% to 60%. The CLIP encoder, 32-token Q-Former, and joint next-token/binary-cross-entropy objectives remain.

E1.justification: Reported pretraining coverage expands from Share-GPT captioning data to a mixture also including CC3M/12M, LAION-400M, and COCO, substantially broadening the training sources (v1 Section 3.2; v2 Section 4.2). The principal evaluation tasks remain VHs, RetVQA, and single-image QA. VizWiz disappears from the main model comparison but remains in the compression experiment, so its coverage is not wholly removed.

E2.justification: V2 adds an OWLv2 detector oracle and evaluates Qwen2-VL, Phi-3 Vision, InternVL2, mPLUG-Owl3, LongVILA, and Idefics3 on VHs, while dropping standalone LLaVA and Claude-3 Opus from that comparison. Caption aggregation changes from LLaVA plus Llama3 to Qwen2-VL plus Llama-v3.1, and CLIP plus LLaVA gains an end-to-end VHs accuracy comparison. V2 Table 1 also omits MI-BART and Qwen-VL-Chat from v1's conventional-benchmark comparison.

E3.justification: V1 uses the 100-question VHs_small subset throughout its main VHs evaluation; v2 uses the full dataset for haystacks of at most 100 images and the small subset for larger haystacks. Single-needle dataset size changes from 880 to 1,000 questions, and multi-needle construction changes from two–five relevant images to two–three. V2 also adds a controlled one/two/three-needle oracle experiment and reports training on 16 rather than eight A100 GPUs.

E4.justification: V2 extends the existing oracle comparisons by separately examining performance with one, two, and three relevant images in Figure 3(A), and expands positional-bias testing to newer models. Appendix A adds object-frequency analysis, and Table C.1 identifies Idefics3's answer-format failures. The compression ablation and retrieval/runtime analysis are retained from v1 rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions use bootstrapped averages. V1 gives a general 3–4% standard-deviation range and specifies 75 observations per bootstrap sample; v2 reports condition-specific standard deviations and graphical error bars but omits that resample-size detail. This refines uncertainty reporting without establishing an increase in independent runs or seeds.

E6.justification: The revised MIRAGE results include RetVQA 70.8 to 67.6, VQAv2 70.0 to 76.6, and MM-Vet 25.8 to 33.4 (v1 Table 3; v2 Table 1). VHs results are extensively replaced under changed model and evaluation conditions—for example, single-needle N=100 changes from 55% to 61.99%, which is not a matched-setting gain. V2 adds many result entries and removes multi-needle N=10,000 results. It also places v1's GPT-4 VQAv2/TextVQA values under GPT-4o without explanation; the compression-ablation values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The retrieval formulation, minimal relevant-image subset, and Equation (1) are retained. Neither version provides substantive theoretical guarantees or proofs, and the revised architectural explanations do not introduce new mathematical results.

C1.justification: V1's headline claims emphasize outperforming GPT-4o by up to 11% and achieving up to 3.4-fold efficiency gains. V2 instead emphasizes up to 13% superiority over open-source LMMs, processing 10,000 images on one 40GB A100, and a new RetVQA state of the art. The RetVQA claim is unsupported by the supplied comparison: v2 reports 67.6 while omitting v1's MI-BART result of 76.5.

C2.justification: V1 attributes MIRAGE's multi-needle advantage over Gemini to multi-image training; v2 instead emphasizes unresolved cross-image reasoning weaknesses relative to Gemini. V2 adds training-data hypotheses for oracle and positional failures and qualifies caption aggregation as query-unaware. It removes the discussion of query-aware retrieval preventing efficient LSH/k-nearest-neighbor indexing. The COCO, template, and societal limitations largely move unchanged to Appendix C.

D1.justification: V2 Appendix B adds API snapshot identifiers, checkpoint links, evaluation and caption-aggregation prompts, and detector-baseline implementation details. Training and inference hardware disclosures also change. Conversely, v2 omits v1's explicit retrieval threshold, one-epoch count, dataset-license statement, and LLaVA-image exclusion statement. Documentation remains inconsistent: Section 4.2 describes about 600K instruction samples while Figure 5 retains a 1.2M training set, and Table B.1 labels a CLIP checkpoint link as OWLv2. The existing project URL is relocated, not newly introduced.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning against contemporary multimodal and video haystack benchmarks, contrasting their synthetic or out-of-distribution needles and shorter contexts with VHs's natural-image construction. It also discusses newer long-context architectures and adds references supporting modern baselines, pretraining sources, and benchmark-reliability arguments. Most earlier MIQA and retrieval-augmented-generation related work remains.

P1.justification: The title changes from 'Answering Harder Questions About Sets of Images' to 'A Vision-Centric Needle-In-A-Haystack Benchmark.' The abstract, introduction, and substantial portions of the main narrative are rewritten around three model failure modes. Benchmark evaluation becomes a separate section, limitations move to the appendix, and the appendices are reorganized and expanded.

P2.justification: V2 replaces the main VHs tables with line plots and places expanded numerical tables in the appendix, redraws the positional heatmaps, and adds dataset examples, an object-frequency chart, prompt/checkpoint displays, and positional line plots. Its model figure combines the revised architecture with the training-distribution chart previously in v1's appendix. The compression table and retrieval/runtime figure are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the central benchmark evaluation: larger samples and explicit uncertainty improve assessability, while the detector control and needle-count oracle analysis better distinguish retrieval from cross-image reasoning failures. Broader contemporary comparisons and implementation documentation also improve usefulness. These gains are limited by important new problems, especially the RetVQA state-of-the-art claim despite the omitted, stronger MI-BART result, and unreconciled training-set counts. Overall, the benchmark evidence improves, but the revision does not establish a substantial overall quality improvement.
